verdict.rationale: Obsidian ships a documented, public plugin API (obsidian-api on GitHub, TypeScript-based) and an Obsidian URI protocol that lets external processes trigger actions like opening or creating notes, giving AI-native users a path to drive the app programmatically. However, this is plugin/TypeScript-centric rather than a native REST/agent API, requires disabling the default Restricted Mode that blocks third-party code execution, and community evidence flags that plugins run with full unsandboxed filesystem/network access rather than a safe automation surface. Missing for 10: a first-party REST/HTTP API designed for external agent control, and independent confirmation of AI agents successfully driving Obsidian via this API.
